        Charles covers crime, policing, justice, and social issues, providing expert analysis on the UK’s most pressing domestic news

Kemi Badenoch has pledged to end Labour’s prison early release schemes.

The Conservative Party leader vowed to force criminals to serve at least half their sentences in jail, and end a Labour change that prevented convicted criminals from being jailed for less than a year.

Such changes would reinstate rules governing the time served behind bars by prisoners. These were in place before Labour freed thousands of inmates who had served 40 per cent of their sentences in its first early release scheme.

The Tories claimed their changes would see up to 80,000 criminals a year spending longer in prison by repealing key planks of the Sentencing Act 2026. The party has also said it would build 50,000 new prison spaces within seven years of taking power, using a £2bn-a-year ring-fenced pot of money.

Mrs Badenoch said: “Victims of horrific crimes live with the consequences every day, but somehow criminals seem to be getting a better deal. Families left terrified by burglaries and violent attacks suffer while those responsible get chance after chance.

“When criminals believe they can get away with breaking the law, there is a collapse in consequences. Prison should mean real punishment, not a slap on the wrist or revolving door where sentences are cut short because Labour can’t find enough cells.

“Labour seems more concerned about getting criminals out of prison than making them face up to the crimes they choose to commit. Sentences must actually mean something in order to keep law-abiding people safe.”

The Tories estimate that the reversal of Labour’s sentencing changes would require an extra 11,000 prison places, above the current 89,000 in prisons in England and Wales.

Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary, who will tell a Westminster audience the 50,000 new places would enable a Tory government to “end Labour’s early release schemes once and for all and bring back shorter sentences to lock up criminals like shoplifters”.

The Government replaced the first version of its early release scheme last month with its “progression” model, under which criminals became eligible for release a third of the way through their sentence, rather than 40 per cent, and halfway, rather than two-thirds, for more serious offences.

The change was applied retrospectively, with the sentences of some 4,500 prisoners recalculated, allowing them to be freed in a series of waves between Oct 1 and June next year.

Andy Burnham was forced to exclude killers, rapists and child sex groomers from the early release scheme after an outcry over the disclosure by The Telegraph that the killers of Pc Andrew Harper would be eligible to be freed early.

The Tories said 82,411 offenders who would have benefited from the changes would now serve at least half their sentences behind bars, or two-thirds for the most serious.

Ending the presumption against short sentences of under a year would require an extra 1,800 prison places, according to the Tories’ analysis. Judges are required to suspend jail terms of under one year rather than send convicted criminals to prison.

The party pledged to end “soft justice”, which it claimed had seen criminals avoiding jail under sentencing guidelines. It also claimed nearly 4,000 offenders convicted of violence had avoided prison in 2024.

For thieves, the party claimed prison had all but vanished, with shoplifting virtually decriminalised. Last year, more than 1,100 convicted thieves with more than 75 previous convictions managed to avoid jail.

A Conservative Party spokesman said: “Short sentences were the tool judges used to take prolific shoplifters off the high street, and Labour have taken it away.”

A Labour Party spokesman said: “The Tories left the prison system in complete disarray and now they want you to forget it. Labour won’t let them. We are determined to do everything possible to keep the most serious offenders behind bars, while preventing the prison system we inherited from collapsing.

“Across 14 years in government, the Tories added just 500 prison places. Now they’re expecting the British people to believe the laughable claim that they’ll build 50,000.

“Labour is fixing the broken system the Tories left behind, with the largest prison building programme since the Victorian era, so victims of crime get the justice they deserve.”
